title: Deponent Verbs
subtitle: loquor, locūtus sum. Passive in form, active in meaning.
objectives: Recognize deponent verbs by their passive forms.
Conjugate common deponents (loquor, sequor, patior, morior, etc.).

sections.heading: Deponent verbs
sections.body:
Deponent verbs have passive forms but active meanings.

loquor, loquī, locūtus sum — to speak
sequor, sequī, secūtus sum — to follow
patior, patī, passus sum — to suffer, endure
morior, morī, mortuus sum — to die

Present: loquor, loqueris, loquitur, loquimur, loquiminī, loquuntur
Perfect: locūtus sum, locūtus es, etc.

Cicero writes: dē hāc rē loquor. — I speak about this matter.
Caesar writes: hostēs secūtī sunt. — They followed the enemies.

items.answer: loquor, loqueris, loquitur, loquimur, loquiminī, loquuntur
Passive in form, active in meaning.
